annotations.annotation_text: Page 267 opens Book 2, Chapter 2 ("The Night Lessons") during the Age of Heroes phase. This passage continues the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes, featuring Shem (Dolph), Shaun (Kev), Issy (footnotes). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8

annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "waves" on page 267 ("The Night Lessons"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during the children studying the Trivium and Quadrivium, Dolph and Kev drawing geometric diagrams of ALP's body, marginal glosses and footnotes. In this Age of Heroes passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 267 ("The Night Lessons"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Heroes dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
